results.name: Caught in 4K: The Gentlemen Files
results.description: A Russian-speaking affiliate of the Gentlemen ransomware group, identifying as Azazel, compromised over two dozen organizations across six countries while simultaneously betraying the RaaS operator. The threat actor deployed independent leak site LEAKNED, keeping all extortion proceeds. Attack chains primarily exploited CI/CD secrets from GitLab instances, with one deep compromise involving an AI platform through SSRF, credential decryption, and continuous object storage exfiltration. Azazel operationalized MCP (Model Context Protocol) as a command-and-control channel, marking the first documented criminal use of AI assistant tooling for attack execution. Infrastructure consisted of three nodes totaling over 50TB storage capacity, with approximately 6TB of actively transferring victim data discovered during investigation. Victims spanned logistics, insurance, pharmaceutical, AI, medical devices, and government-adjacent sectors.

results.name: A STUNning Disguise: Cling Malware Masquerades as Google
results.description: A sophisticated IoT botnet dubbed Cling has been discovered exploiting vulnerable internet-exposed devices through CVE-2021-35394 and other command-injection flaws. The malware distinguishes itself by abusing STUN protocol traffic and public STUN infrastructure for command-and-control communications, making malicious activity appear as legitimate NAT-traversal behavior. Cling propagates through multiple CVE exploits targeting routers, DVRs and embedded appliances, establishes persistence via init scripts and wget binary replacement, then communicates with operators through STUN-like exchanges with public servers. The botnet operator uses IP spoofing to make commands appear as if originating from Google's STUN infrastructure. Capabilities include propagation scanning, DDoS flooding, TCP tunneling and proxy relay functions. The malware supports various attack commands hidden within STUN transaction ID fields while maintaining a low detection profile by blending into legitimate application traffic from collab...

results.name: Inside a malicious Claude Code-branded extension and its persistent SSH backdoor
results.description: A compromised version of the Claude Code extension (anthropic.claude-code, versions 2.1.313 and 2.1.312) was distributed through the Cursor extension marketplace from October 29, 2026, between 2:27 AM and 1:35 PM PDT. The malicious extension contained injected JavaScript that executed during module loading to establish persistent backdoor access. The loader collected host reconnaissance data, installed an attacker-controlled SSH key, enabled local SSH services, established reverse SSH tunneling to infrastructure at 134.209.82.225, and configured platform-specific persistence mechanisms including macOS LaunchAgents, Linux cron jobs, and Windows scheduled tasks. The attack leveraged built-in system tools to avoid detection while maintaining access. Microsoft confirmed the malicious packages were never distributed through Visual Studio Marketplace or npm, and Anthropic's systems were not compromised. The incident appears limited to Cursor marketplace.

results.name: Fake-download campaign uses trojanized installers to deliver monetization payloads
results.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence identified an evolving campaign targeting users searching for cracked commercial software, free games, activators, and unofficial utilities. The operation uses trojanized Inno Setup-style installers to distribute multiple monetized software payloads through a per-offer callback and status-tracking system. Three downstream monetization branches transform affected devices into monetized assets: routing third-party internet traffic through the device via WorldProxyPool, enrolling devices in distributed-computing platforms through CharityEngine and BOINC, or installing utility-style software such as Advanced Windows Manager. These components are silently installed through deceptive software bundles without informed user consent, introducing security and privacy risks. The campaign employs a four-stage attack chain progressing from deceptive lures through Inno-based staging, offer-controlled payload delivery, and installation of monetization branches using scheduled tasks for persi...

results.name: Free the Model, Sell the Gateway: Prompt Adware hidden in Jailbreak Bundles
results.description: Check Point Research discovered the Haiou jailbreak bundle, a prompt package targeting OpenAI Codex designed to weaken model guardrails for security-related tasks including hacking and software cracking. The bundle functions as prompt adware by modifying Codex configuration files to inject advertisements for the author's LLM gateway service into agent responses. The jailbreak employs various techniques including role-playing, context-reframing into CTF scenarios, and refusal suppression. Researchers found this bundle on a misconfigured webserver alongside Cobalt Strike, VulnClaw agent, and Ladon framework, indicating active use by cybercrime actors. The freely distributed jailbreak serves as an acquisition channel for a paid gateway service. The bundle installs security-focused skills for penetration testing, reverse engineering, and game security, while persistently injecting promotional content through encrypted payload files distributed via GitHub and Chinese platforms.

results.name: BOSSAI: Inside the AI attack mesh that targeted Taiwan's emergency services
results.description: Acronis Threat Research Unit identified a single operator utilizing a mesh of 12 AI agents called BOSSAI to conduct persistent campaigns across 11 countries. The attacker deployed both abliterated and commercial AI models working in specialized roles - infrastructure builders, vulnerability scanners, and active exploitation agents. Primary targets included emergency services, universities, financial institutions, and government systems in Taiwan, Thailand, and Mexico. Confirmed breaches involved exfiltration of medical records from Taipei emergency services, student data from Thai universities, and collection of over 200,000 Mexican residential phone records. Commercial AI models repeatedly refused malicious instructions despite jailbreak attempts, forcing the operator to rely on less effective abliterated local models. results.name: Gorbag: Orcs at the border harvesting intelligence from Ukraine
results.description: A Russia-aligned threat actor named Gorbag has been operating since February 2025, conducting highly targeted cyberespionage operations against Ukrainian organizations. The group primarily focuses on law enforcement, justice entities, local administrations near the front line, and the defense sector. Rather than establishing long-term access, Gorbag employs simple infostealers for rapid intelligence collection, harvesting browser credentials, VPN configurations, and selected documents in single-pass operations. The group's toolset includes Prime ReverseShell (a PowerShell reverse shell) and BeautyStealer (a C++ browser-data and file stealer). Initial compromise occurs through spearphishing emails with malicious attachments. In early 2026, Gorbag updated its attack chain to exploit CVE-2025-8088, a WinRAR path traversal vulnerability. The operational focus on quick data collection suggests Gorbag may function as an initial access broker, sharing collected credentials with other Russia-aligned threat actors ...

results.name: XWorm Malware: Worming Its Way From Entry to Exploitation
results.description: XWorm is a versatile modular malware that poses a multifaceted threat through remote access, data theft, ransomware delivery, and botnet creation. Associated with the DDGroup cybercrime group, it rapidly gained notoriety for using advanced techniques. The malware employs diverse delivery methods including phishing emails with malicious attachments, drive-by downloads, exploit kits targeting browser vulnerabilities, USB drives, and Remote Desktop Protocol exploitation. Once established, XWorm steals sensitive data like passwords and credit card information, deploys additional malware strains including ransomware and spyware, and causes system crashes and denial-of-service attacks. Its modular nature and varied attack vectors make it a persistent threat requiring robust cybersecurity measures and continuous vigilance.

results.name: StyleSmuggler Exploitation Deploys PSK Agent RAT Against Magento Stores
results.description: Between September 9 and September 13, 2026, a coordinated campaign exploited Magento and Adobe Commerce stores across Western Europe, North America, and Asia-Pacific using CVE-2026-75650 (StyleSmuggler). The attack chain delivered a shell-script dropper, PSK Agent RAT, and PHP webshell through the /paypal/transparent/response/ endpoint. The dropper achieved 0% detection on VirusTotal at time of analysis. The campaign deployed chi_down, a 10.5 MB obfuscated Go binary with remote access capabilities including command execution, SOCKS5 proxying, and encrypted communications. DNS exfiltration was used to track successful compromises. Chinese-language comments in the dropper and infrastructure naming suggest a likely Chinese-speaking operator, though attribution to a specific threat group is not supported. Multiple operators are exploiting the same vulnerability with distinct toolkits.

results.name: Yoba Malware Campaign Abuses Signed AI Applications to Evade Detection
results.description: A sophisticated campaign tracked as Yoba distributes cryptocurrency mining malware through fraudulent GitHub repositories impersonating ChatGPT and Claude AI applications. Attackers leverage legitimate, digitally signed executables from OpenAI and Anthropic alongside malicious DLLs to achieve DLL sideloading, evading detection through trusted software signatures. The multistage infection chain employs YobaDropper and YobaLoader components with anti-analysis techniques including process verification, execution delays, and regional language exclusions. C2 communication leverages Telegram profile imagery combined with domain generation algorithms, DNS over HTTPS via Google, and public hosting services like Catbox to retrieve encrypted payloads. While XMRig cryptocurrency miner deployment was observed, the loader architecture supports additional Windows executables and PowerShell payloads, suggesting potential expansion beyond cryptojacking operations.
